title: Vasco-Margao iron ore mining: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**Iron ore mining is a capital-heavy extraction business that converts a finite ore body into saleable tonnes, and cash arrives only when those tonnes move by rail or road to steel mills.** The value sits in the mining lease and statutory clearances, not in the plant; ICRA calls mining 'highly capital-intensive' [5] and the sector 'highly regulated' with mandatory environmental impact assessment, forest clearance and coastal provisions [8]. So when a proposal lands, check the lease, the environmental clearance and the mining plan first; if any is pending or under renewal, ask for the current sanctioned capacity and stop there.

## Where cash and value sit
**Realisation per tonne is the swing factor, and it is falling even for good operators.** SMIORE's average realisation fell 17% y-o-y to INR 3,095/t in Q1FY'27 [4], after holding at INR 2,834/t in FY'26 [2]. Production capacity was raised to 4.45 mnt/y from 1.6 mnt/y [4], so volume growth is real but price is not. **Working capital sits in royalty and statutory dues paid upfront and in receivables from steel mills; capex sits in haulage, beneficiation and rail linkage.** NMDC's rail connectivity improvements are cited as strengthening its logistics backbone [1] — for a Goa borrower, ask who owns the evacuation route and what it costs per tonne; collect from customer.

## What has changed now
**Peer results are strong on volume and mixed on price.** NMDC posted 20% production growth in FY'26 and targets around 60 mnt in FY'27 [1]; SMIORE's FY'26 output rose 14% to 4.35 mnt [2] and Q1FY'27 output rose 27% y-o-y [4]. SMIORE's Q1FY'27 revenue rose 27% to INR 55.4 billion with EBITDA up 8% to INR 23.7 billion [3]. **The sources say almost nothing about Vasco-Margao or Goa specifically, so lean on first principles and these peers.** The official data pack returns no score for this industry in this state [D]; treat that as an absence of evidence, not a clean bill.

## Who to pursue, who to avoid
**Pursue permitted merchant miners with an approved capacity already at or near their maximum permitted annual output, as SMIORE reports for Q1FY'27 [3], and captive-linked miners feeding their own steel, the model ICRA describes for SMIORE and ASPL [6].** Avoid lease-holders still awaiting clearances, single-mine borrowers with no evacuation tie-up, and anyone whose realisation assumption is above INR 3,095/t [4]. **Structure on tonnage and realisation, not on projected prices.** Take monthly: production and dispatch tonnages, average realisation per tonne, royalty and statutory dues paid, and stock at pit-head and port.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch realisation first.** If average realisation falls below the prior quarter, ask for the buyer-wise price list and re-run the debt-service cover on the lower number. If dispatch falls while production holds, ore is stuck — check stock and evacuation. If statutory dues age beyond the licence cycle, the lease itself is at risk [8]. Rating reports here are undated [5][6][7][8]; the April 2024 ICRA note [7] is old and should not anchor a 2026 decision.
watch: Dispatch falls two months running while output holds -> ask for stock statement and evacuation contract
Falls below INR 3,095/t [4] -> re-run cover on the lower price and seek promoter support
Dues unpaid beyond one licence cycle -> freeze fresh limits and review lease standing [8]
Any clearance under renewal -> hold disbursement until renewed [8]
